Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026 – 9–11 October, Marina Bay Street Circuit (Singapore's first F1 Sprint weekend)

2. Singapore History Gallery reopens – 10 October, National Museum of Singapore (free 139th anniversary celebrations, 10–18 October)

3. Amber Lounge Singapore – 10–11 October, The Fullerton Bay Hotel (Official Formula 1 Afterparty)

4. Grand Prix Season Singapore continues citywide – Orchard Paddock, Porsche Raceborn Fest and more through 11 October

5. NOOR Singapore – new Mediterranean and Japanese restaurant, Mohamed Sultan Road

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

This is race week. The Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026 runs 9–11 October at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, the city's first F1 Sprint weekend, with Padang Stage headliners JJ Lin, The Killers and Lana Del Rey. Around it, Grand Prix Season Singapore fills the city with race-themed programming through 11 October, while Amber Lounge takes over The Fullerton Bay Hotel's Clifford Pier for the weekend's Official Formula 1 Afterparty. Away from the track, the National Museum reopens its Singapore History Gallery on 10 October, its first full revamp since 2006, with nine days of free anniversary celebrations. Expect the city, and especially the Marina Centre and Padang area, to be considerably busier and more congested than usual all week – see Transport & Operational Updates for full details.

Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026

Singapore's marquee event of the year returns to the Marina Bay Street Circuit, and 2026 brings a genuine first: the city's inaugural F1 Sprint weekend. The music is part of the ticket. Every race ticket includes Zone 4, home of the Padang Stage, where JJ Lin and CORTIS play on Friday; The Killers, returning after eight years, and Zara Larsson on Saturday; and James Arthur followed by Lana Del Rey, in her first-ever Singapore concert, on Sunday. Zone 1 has its own stages, the Wharf Stage (Split Enz, Goo Goo Dolls and Janet Jackson) and the new Barge Stage (Mark Ronson, DJ Snake, Major Lazer Soundsystem and more), and needs a Zone 1 ticket. Tickets are day-specific.

Event Date: 9–11 October 2026
Location: Marina Bay Street Circuit
Admission: Ticketed via singaporegp.sg; several ticket categories have sold out. Three-day Zone 4 walkabout tickets start from S$548
Best For: Motorsport Fans / Concertgoers / Once-a-year Atmosphere

Concierge Recommendation: Guests without tickets can still catch plenty of the atmosphere through Grand Prix Season Singapore's precinct events (see below). For guests attending the race, the last trains from City Hall MRT are extended on race nights (12:30am on 9 and 10 October, 12:45am on 11 October) – worth mentioning when they plan their evenings.

Grand Prix Season Singapore – Race-Week Activations

Grand Prix Season Singapore's 17th edition runs through 11 October, spreading race-season energy well beyond the circuit. The final week brings its busiest run of precinct programming:

  • Orchard Paddock 2026 – Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza, 8–10 October. Late-night dining, live performances, car-themed challenges and open-air movies, with ALYPH and YAØ headlining the music on 8 October.

  • Porsche Raceborn Fest – Guoco Midtown, 130 Beach Road, 9–11 October. Classic Porsche racing cars on display, the Southeast Asian unveiling of the new 911 Challenge race car, and professional racing simulators.

  • Ray-Ban presents: Beyond the Track – CQ @ Clarke Quay, through 14 October. Scuderia Ferrari Collection showcase, racing simulators and a Pit Stop Challenge, with an appearance by a Scuderia Ferrari HP Formula 1 driver.

  • adidas Motorsport Popups – Funan and Raffles City Shopping Centre, through 12 October. Show-car displays and racing simulators, including a replica Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 car at the Raffles City entrance.

  • Sago Festival of Speed – Duxton Hill, 10 October, 1:00pm–6:00pm. Free block party with classic cars and motorcycles, street food and an F1 simulator ($49 per 10-minute session, 20 slots).

Amber Lounge Singapore

Race week's most exclusive after-dark fixture returns to Clifford Pier at The Fullerton Bay Hotel for two nights as the Official Formula 1 Afterparty, presented by Moët & Chandon. Founded in Monaco in 2003 and now in its 23rd year across Monaco, Singapore and Abu Dhabi, Amber Lounge is a private social theatre rather than a conventional nightclub; guests in past years have included Formula 1 drivers Charles Leclerc, Fernando Alonso and Lewis Hamilton. Saturday features apl.de.ap and J. Rey Soul of the Black Eyed Peas, and Eve headlines on Sunday.

Event Date: 10 and 11 October 2026, doors at 9:00pm each night, until 5:00am
Location: Clifford Pier, The Fullerton Bay Hotel, 80 Collyer Quay
Admission: Club Pass from S$850 per person; booked directly at amberlounge.com, no circuit ticket needed. Shared and private tables available at higher tiers for groups.
Dress Code: Smart elegant, strictly enforced – collared shirts and tailored trousers for gentlemen, cocktail or evening wear for ladies; no sportswear, trainers, shorts or casual denim
Age Restriction: 18 and above; valid photo ID required at check-in
Best For: VIP Guests / Nightlife / Race-Week Glamour

Concierge Recommendation: The single most-asked-about race-week evening for VIP guests. Amber Lounge advises booking before race week, as the most sought-after tables sell early and the room does not expand for late demand. The Fullerton Bay Hotel's concierge team manages vehicle access for its own guests on the night.

Singapore History Gallery Reopens – Stories of Everyday

The National Museum of Singapore reopens its flagship Singapore History Gallery on 10 October, its first full revamp since it opened in 2006. The revamp traces more than 700 years of Singapore's history, from 14th-century Temasek to today, through the voices of people who lived it. New additions include a restored 1970s HDB lift, a traditional Nanyang coffee-roasting machine and a newly commissioned timelapse work by photographer Keith Loutit. The reopening comes two days before the Museum's 139th anniversary, marked by nine days of free celebrations called Stories of Everyday, with installations, an art market, live performances and workshops, and the debut of the Museum's new mascot, Stoney, inspired by the Singapore Stone.

Event Date: Gallery reopens 10 October; Stories of Everyday runs 10–18 October 2026, 10am–7pm (last entry to the galleries 6:30pm)
Location: National Museum of Singapore, 93 Stamford Road, Singapore 178897
Admission: Free entry to the anniversary celebrations for everyone; the permanent galleries are free for Singaporeans and PRs, with standard admission for other visitors
Best For: History Lovers / Families / Culture-Minded Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A good indoor, air-conditioned option for guests wanting a break from race-week crowds, and a strong introduction to Singapore's history for international guests. Stamford Road is among the roads affected by the Grand Prix closures, so guests are best sent by MRT with extra time allowed.

F1 The Exhibition

Asia's first stop for this touring exhibition, produced in partnership with Formula 1, fills a purpose-built tent at Gardens by the Bay with seven themed rooms covering the sport's 76-year history: iconic race cars including the 2011 championship-winning Red Bull RB7, driver artefacts, race suits and helmets, and a Singapore-only experience called Singapore Drive. Singapore is its 11th host city. Racing simulators are available as an add-on.

Event Date: Through 18 October 2026. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 11:00am–8:00pm; closed Monday
Location: Eastern Greenway, Gardens by the Bay, next to Satay by the Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive (Gardens by the Bay MRT, Exit 1)
Admission: Adults $49, ages 13–17 $40, ages 5–12 $29, via Ticketek; simulator add-on $20
Best For: F1 Fans / Families / Guests Without Race Tickets

Concierge Recommendation: A good alternative for guests who could not secure race tickets. Allow around 90 minutes, and note that it closes on 18 October and is shut on Mondays.

Also This Week

  • Jiaoying Summers – Capitol Theatre, 6 October, evening. The China-born, Austin-based comedian's Lucky Pony Tour, for one night only as part of Just For Laughs Singapore. Tickets $68–$128.

  • Art Remembers – National Gallery Singapore, through 18 October. Twenty contemporary works by Southeast Asian artists explore how archives can reframe forgotten and marginalised histories, in the Singtel Special Exhibition Gallery 1 and City Hall Chamber. General admission ticket required; free for Singaporeans and PRs.

  • Singapore Symphony Orchestra pre-tour concerts – University Cultural Centre, National University of Singapore, 7:30pm on 8 and 9 October. Chloe Chua & Hannu Lintu – Jewel and Titan (8 October) and Mozart's Sinfonia Concertante and Mahler's Titan (9 October), ahead of the orchestra's China tour.

Restaurants & Bars

NOOR Singapore

A Mediterranean and Japanese kitchen and bar that opened on 1 July in the River Valley pocket of Mohamed Sultan Road. Led by chef and co-owner Titus Thamil, the menu runs on tahini, labneh and harissa with Japanese touches folded in: miso in the hummus, yuzu in the labneh, shawarma-spiced chicken in gyoza wrappers, and a house Shok Bread that is NOOR's take on shokupan. The 65-seat room has warm terracotta walls, a small izakaya-style hideaway at the back, and themed nights with music.

Location: 17 Mohamed Sultan Road, Singapore 238966 (about six minutes' walk from Fort Canning MRT)
Hours: Tuesday to Sunday, 5:00pm–midnight; closed Monday
Reservations: via NOOR's website or +65 8805 8075
Best For: Groups / Date Night / Fusion Cuisine Fans

Concierge Recommendation: A good pick for guests who want a long, sociable dinner rather than a quick one. The menu is built for sharing and the restaurant encourages a slow evening; ask about the themed nights when booking.

Mukai

A Shibuya-born seafood-bowl specialist whose Plaza Singapura outlet, opened in August, is its first outside Japan. The signature Kaiho Don ("sea treasure") is seafood chopped and stacked high over seasoned sushi rice, eaten cold first and then finished with warm dashi poured over the remainder to turn it into ochazuke. Bowls start from $28.90++, with a limited Goku Goku bowl at $79.90++ capped at 30 a day.

Location: #B1-07, Plaza Singapura, 68 Orchard Road, Singapore 238839 (connected to Dhoby Ghaut MRT)
Hours: Daily, 11:30am–3:00pm and 5:30pm–10:00pm
Best For: Seafood Lovers / Solo Diners / Orchard Road Lunch
Note: Not halal-certified

Concierge Recommendation: A good solo or small-group meal on Orchard Road, with counter seating facing the chefs. The dashi pour-over is the part guests tend to remember.

Katsu by Kyu

Singapore's first tonkatsu restaurant to use Jeju pork exclusively, opened in July at OUE Downtown Gallery. Each cut is dry-aged for 10 days, breaded in panko mixed with freshly milled rice powder and finished over rice-straw charcoal, and sets come with freshly milled Korean rice cooked in iron pots. The 44-seat room takes its cues from a Korean hanok, with counter seats around the open kitchen.

Location: #01-09, OUE Downtown Gallery, 6A Shenton Way, Singapore 068815 (about three minutes' walk from Tanjong Pagar MRT)
Hours: Monday to Saturday, 11:00am–3:00pm and 5:00pm–10:00pm; closed Sunday
Signature: Jeju pork tonkatsu – Tenderloin $30, Loin $32, Central-Cut Premium Loin $38
Best For: Tonkatsu Fans / Business Lunch / Something Different
Note: Not halal-certified

Concierge Recommendation: Worth mentioning to guests who already know Japanese tonkatsu and are curious about the Korean approach. The open-kitchen counter is the best seat, and the restaurant is closed on Sundays.

LingZhi Greens

A Chinese vegetarian name since 1991, LingZhi has moved from Liat Towers to Palais Renaissance and reopened on 10 August as LingZhi Greens. Led by Executive Chef Michael Huang, the refreshed menu centres on whole foods, premium vegetables and wild mushrooms rather than mock meat, in a Song Dynasty-inspired space. Its vegetarian take on Peking duck, with vegetarian goose and crispy beancurd skin in a wheat wrap, is the dish to know.

Location: #B1-04/05, Palais Renaissance, 390 Orchard Road, Singapore 238871 (beside the Royal Thai Embassy; carpark entrance via Claymore Drive)
Hours: Daily, 11:00am–3:00pm and 6:00pm–10:00pm
Signature: Vegetarian Goose and Crispy Beancurd Skin with Wheat Wrap ($26 for eight pieces); Truffle Mushroom Bisque
Best For: Vegetarian Guests / Health-Conscious Diners
Promotion: LingZhi Pals blind-bag draw with dine-in, 25 August – 30 October 2026, while stocks last

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable option for vegetarian guests who want something more considered than a salad bar. It is about an eight-minute walk from Orchard MRT.

Rempapa

Chef Damian D'Silva's heritage restaurant, serving Eurasian, Peranakan, Malay, Indian and Chinese home cooking, has moved from PLQ to National Gallery Singapore. It is a homecoming for the chef, who spent his early years in the caretaker quarters of what was then the Supreme Court, now part of the Gallery. The Gallery outpost is a casual, self-service concept with 114 seats, serving signature rice bowls, handmade kueh and homemade kaya toast on thick shokupan.

Location: #01-02A, National Gallery Singapore, 1 St Andrew's Road, Singapore 178957
Hours: Daily, 10:00am–7:00pm; walk-ins welcome, no reservation needed
Best For: Heritage Cuisine / Casual Lunch / Gallery Visits

Concierge Recommendation: A natural lunch stop for guests visiting the National Gallery. St Andrew's Road is among the roads closed for the Grand Prix from 7 to 13 October, so guests are best sent by MRT to City Hall with extra time allowed.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Tatsuya @ Goodwood

Chef-owner Ronnie Chia opened Tatsuya in 1998 after honing his craft in Japan, and it remains a fixture of Goodwood Park Hotel. The room is a cosy space of zen pinewood, and guests can sit at the 24-seat sushi bar to watch the chefs at work or choose the more traditional main dining room. Regulars come for the aburi sushi and the Saga Beef Don, a dish long available on request.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: Reservations via SevenRooms; advance booking recommended, particularly for the sushi bar.

Hours: Daily. Lunch 12:00pm–3:00pm; dinner 6:30pm–11:00pm.

Address: Goodwood Park Hotel, 22 Scotts Road, Singapore 228221

Website: https://www.tatsuya.com.sg/

Signature: Aburi Sushi; Saga Beef Don

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable choice for guests who want excellent Japanese food without committing to a long omakase. The sushi-bar seats are worth requesting for first-time visitors.

Cumi Bali

A family-run Indonesian restaurant on Tras Street, halal-certified and a Michelin Bib Gourmand recipient, which began on Duxton Hill before moving to its current home. The namesake Cumi Bali, a whole squid lightly chargrilled and served with a house-made spice sauce, is the reason most guests come. Ayam Sate Madura, a Javanese chicken satay served without peanut sauce, and Nasi Kunyit, a turmeric rice with 11 spices, round out a menu with portions made for sharing.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: Halal-certified; reserve by phone on +65 6220 6619.

Hours: Daily. Lunch 11:30am–2:30pm; dinner 6:00pm–9:30pm.

Address: 50 Tras Street, Singapore 078989

Website: https://www.cumibali.com/

Signature: Cumi Bali (chargrilled squid); Ayam Sate Madura; Nasi Kunyit; Ikan Bakar (fish grilled in an 18-spice paste)

Concierge Recommendation: A good family-friendly recommendation for guests wanting genuine Indonesian flavours without a fine-dining price tag, and a straightforward halal option in Tanjong Pagar.

Hotel & Hospitality News

  • Raffles Sentosa Singapore has appointed William Numa as its new Hotel Manager. Numa brings nearly three decades of international hospitality experience and was most recently resident manager at Cheval Blanc Saint Barth.

  • Naumi Hotel Singapore has appointed Shue Sng as General Manager, effective September 2026. Sng brings close to 20 years of hospitality experience across Singapore and Asia-Pacific, most recently as Group Head of Sales at Soori Hotel & Resorts, and previously led The Warehouse Hotel.

Transport & Operational Updates

Road closures for the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix are in effect from 12:01am on Wednesday, 7 October until 5:30am on Tuesday, 13 October. Affected roads include Nicoll Highway, St Andrew's Road, Raffles Boulevard, Republic Boulevard, Raffles Avenue, Bayfront Avenue, Esplanade Drive, Stamford Road and Bras Basah Road. Selected stretches reopen briefly each morning (5:30am–10:00am) on 7, 8, 9 and 12 October. A single-lane Access Lane along Raffles Boulevard stays open via Nicoll Highway or Temasek Boulevard, except for buses and W, X and Y-plated vehicles; taxis and motorcycles can use it at all times except during track activity hours. Car parks at Suntec City, Millenia Walk and Marina Square remain open throughout.

Trains run later on race nights: the last trains from City Hall MRT leave at 12:30am on 9 and 10 October and 12:45am on 11 October. The nearest MRT stations to the circuit are City Hall, Esplanade, Promenade and Raffles Place. Expect heavy congestion across the city, not only around the circuit, and higher hotel rates and occupancy between 5 and 12 October.

Getting to the circuit: MRT is the recommended way to reach Marina Bay Street Circuit, with nine gates each within walking distance of a station – Gate 1 (Nicoll Highway), Gate 2 (Promenade), Gates 3A/3B (City Hall / Esplanade), Gates 4–6 (Raffles Place), Gate 7 (Esplanade), and Gate 8 (Bayfront). Guests heading to Gate 1 can also use Lavender MRT, which connects to the gate by a short dedicated shuttle service. For guests taking a taxi or private hire, the nearest official drop-off points are along Nicoll Highway for Gate 1; at Conrad Centennial, Pan Pacific Singapore or The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore for Gate 2; and at Marina Bay Sands for Gate 8 – all a short walk from the gate itself, since vehicles cannot approach the gates directly. Once inside the Circuit Park, race organisers also run a shuttle service between distant gates and zones – useful since Zone 1 (Pit, Turn 1–Turn 3) and Zone 4 (Padang, Esplanade Waterfront, Stamford) are a substantial walk apart; look for signage at each zone entrance.

Suggested Itineraries

Race Week Without a Ticket

Morning: Start at the National Museum of Singapore for the reopened Singapore History Gallery and the free Stories of Everyday celebrations – allow at least two hours. Stamford Road is among the roads affected by the race-week closures, so travel by MRT.

Afternoon: Head to Duxton Hill for the Sago Festival of Speed – free to browse, with classic cars and motorcycles, street food and an F1 simulator ($49 per 10-minute session).

Evening: Continue to CQ @ Clarke Quay for Ray-Ban's Beyond the Track activation, then dinner at one of Clarke Quay's riverside restaurants.

Tip: This itinerary works best on Saturday 10 October, the one day the Sago Festival of Speed and the museum's reopening celebrations overlap.

A Grand Prix Weekend

Friday: Visit Porsche's Raceborn Fest at Guoco Midtown (free, 9–11 October) during the day; ticketed guests can catch JJ Lin on the Padang Stage that night.

Saturday: Spend the afternoon at F1 The Exhibition at Gardens by the Bay (open 11am–8pm), then head to Orchard Paddock at Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza (8–10 October) for live music and open-air dining.

Sunday: The Grand Prix takes place in the evening, and ticketed guests can end the night with Lana Del Rey on the Padang Stage. For everyone else, the final day of Porsche's Raceborn Fest is a free daytime option.

Tip: Book dinners well outside the Marina Centre closure zone on all three nights, and allow extra time for taxis and ride-hailing around Marina Bay.

Quick Reference

Best Overall Pick: Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026 (9–11 October)

Best Alternative to a Race Ticket: F1 The Exhibition, Gardens by the Bay

Best Free Cultural Pick: Singapore History Gallery reopening and Stories of Everyday (National Museum)

Best VIP Recommendation: Amber Lounge Singapore (book early)

Best New Restaurant: NOOR Singapore

Best Solo Lunch: Mukai (Plaza Singapura)

Looking Ahead: Grand Prix road closures lift at 5:30am on 13 October
